title: bot.ability.listening.sensitivity.output
description: A received sound paired with its perceived level: the level, in dB, of whatever about this arrival the body's own predictions did not account for.

sound.description: The sound exactly as it was received. Never altered here.

audio.description: Reference (a URI reference) to the audio this stimulus carries; floppy passes media by reference, never as bytes [floppy field].
audio.title: Audio

media_type.description: Optional media type or codec label, such as audio/pcm or audio/opus.
media_type.title: Media Type

sample_rate_hz.description: Optional sample rate for raw or decoded audio, measured in hertz.
sample_rate_hz.title: Sample Rate Hz

channels.description: Optional number of audio channels represented by the chunk.
channels.title: Channels

kind.description: Optional low-cardinality acoustic provenance hint. Prefer domain-qualified labels when the source is clear (for example phone.ringing, phone.call, ambient, knock) so models do not confuse bare tokens like ring. Not a linguistic interpretation.
kind.title: Kind

amplitude_db.description: Optional loudness of this sound at its source, in dB SPL measured one metre away. A shout and a whisper leave the same mouth, so loudness belongs to the sound rather than to the thing that made it. How far it carries is the environment's to work out; omitting this means the sound reaches every listener regardless of distance.
amplitude_db.title: Amplitude Db

received_level_db.description: Optional loudness of this sound in dB SPL where the recipient of this event is, which is a different quantity from amplitude_db: the same shout is one level at the mouth and another at the far side of the room. The environment fills this in per recipient, so an emitter never sets it. None means the environment had nothing to measure — the sound carried no amplitude, or nobody said where it or the listener was — not that the sound was silent.
received_level_db.title: Received Level Db

source.description: Optional acoustic source: the transducer this sound came off, as its emitter stamps it (speaking stamps its mouth, "speaking", the mouth its efference copy names). The original carries it as the sound event's source; an SCXML event relayed through the body keeps only its data, so floppy carries it in the sound [floppy field]. Listening scores an arrival against an efference copy only when this is the producing mouth; a sound without one is never the bot's own.
source.title: Source

participants.description: Who produced this stimulus, stamped by the device that emitted it. Empty when the device knows no one (ambient sound, an unattended camera).

items.description: Someone who took part in a stimulus: an opaque, producer-stable identity reference and the role it played (source: who produced it; target: who it was addressed to).

ref.description: Opaque, producer-stable identity such as a phone number, an app person id, or a chat handle. Never a display name chosen by the bot.
ref.title: Ref

role.description: source: who produced the stimulus (speaker, sender). target: who it was addressed to.
role.title: Role

own.description: True when the producer knows this participant is the bot itself, for example the bot's own voice heard back or the voice it spoke with. Stamped only by that producer; never inferred.
own.title: Own

resembles.description: For an identity its producer made just now (nobody it knew): the known identities it resembles, best first, at most 3. Stamped only by that producer; never a link.

items.description: A known identity this new one resembles: its ref and how similar the two are (-1..1). Perception data only: it links nothing, and it is never a print.

ref.description: The ref of the known identity, as its producer stamps it.
ref.title: Ref

similarity.description: How similar the two are, -1..1; higher is more alike.
similarity.title: Similarity

resembles.title: Resembles

items.title: Participant

participants.title: Participants

sound.title: SoundData

event.description: Canonical HSM event name that emitted this upstream payload.
event.title: Event

data.description: Complete typed payload emitted by the upstream event.

parent.description: The exact environment.sound event and payload that produced this scored sound. This is domain provenance, not telemetry metadata or an actor lookup.

perceived_level_db.description: Level in dB of the part of this arrival that nothing predicted — what perception is actually left with. With nothing predicting it, that is the whole sound, so this is the level it arrived at. Fully predicted, nothing is left and this is 0.0. Predicted but off by some margin, that margin is what survives. None means there was no level to work from, which is not the same as silence: an unmeasurable arrival cannot be shown to be quiet and must be treated as heard.
perceived_level_db.title: Perceived Level Db
